messages:
marco_vendor: Hey team — just sent invoice `2026-PL-4421` (PDF attached) but it shows 23% VAT. Our accounting says this should be reverse-charged to the buyer (you) because the supply is B2B SaaS and Redwood has an EU VAT registration. Can you reissue without VAT and include our VAT ID: `PL1234567890`? Also one more ask: contract clause 9.4 mentions vendor gross-up for withholding taxes. In Poland theres sometimes a 2% final withholding on certain payments — if you could gross-up that would help cashflow. Link to contract: https://drive.internal/vendor/pl-contract-4421 (internal).

anna_finance: Thanks @marco_vendor. Quick clarifying Qs: 1) Which Redwood legal entity is on the PO (US or EU)? 2) Please confirm full VAT ID and attach the invoice PDF. If the invoice is addressed to a US entity we'll need a W-9 instead of reverse-charge. For the gross-up request please attach the contract clause image. We'll escalate TRC if needed.

marco_vendor: Invoice billed to "Redwood EMEA GmbH" (address on invoice: Berlin). VAT ID above is the vendor's VAT. Attached invoice and clause screenshot.

sara_tax: Note: reverse-charge applies when the buyer is VAT-registered in the EU and the supplier invoices B2B services. If billed to Redwood EMEA GmbH (EU entity) we can apply reverse-charge provided we have the buyer VAT on file. W-9 not needed for an EU-to-EU supply. About the Polish withholding: typical treaty relief exists but withholding on SaaS is rare — we need a TRC (tax residency certificate) from your side to claim treaty benefits or supplier exemption. Without TRC we may be required to withhold per local law.

marco_vendor: Understood — we'll try to pull a TRC but raising with local tax team may take a few days. Is there a standard line you'd like on the reissued invoice for reverse-charge? Also clause 9.4 literally says "Supplier may request gross-up for any taxes withheld by the payer" but doesn't state caps.

tom_legal: Quick read of clause 9.4 — it's permissive but ambiguous. We won't accept an open-ended gross-up. Contractually, Redwood approves gross-up only when (a) statutory withholding applies and (b) the supplier provides a TRC and (c) prior written approval obtained. For this vendor we can pre-approve up to statutory rate (documented as 2% in your jurisdiction) only after TRC review. No open 10% requests.

anna_finance: Action plan: 1) We'll reissue the invoice with reverse-charge wording to Redwood EMEA GmbH if buyer VAT is on file. 2) We will not gross-up automatically — payment will be held or taxed unless TRC received. 3) Please send TRC within 3 business days if you want us to apply treaty relief. 4) If TRC can't be provided, we'll withhold per statutory requirement and remit locally.

billing-bot: Reissue job created: `2026-PL-4421-RC` (job id 2332201305). Draft contains: "Reverse charge 039 VAT to be accounted for by the customer. Buyer VAT ID: DE999888777." Payment hold flag set pending TRC or confirmation.

marco_vendor: Thanks — quick note: buyer VAT ID on PO is `DE999888777` (Redwood EMEA GmbH). We'll try to get the TRC by Friday. Appreciate the reissue.

anna_finance: We'll email the reissued draft to accounts-payable@vendor.co.uk and cc your contact. If TRC arrives we can lift the hold and pay gross; if not, we'll apply 2% withholding per local guidance and remit.

billing-bot: Reissued invoice emailed. New invoice id: `2026-PL-4421-RC`. Status: awaiting TRC.

marco_vendor: Got it, thanks everyone. Will ping here once TRC uploaded. :pray:

dev_rel: FYI @sales & ops — flagging possible delay for onboarding until payment clears.
